## Introduction
### Fundamentals of network
Note : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sH4JCwjybGs is the video link
++list
- 1) Ip-address
-- a) ipv4 is still used but by using nat(network translation), we can dynamically map ipaddresses to certain local devices without ever assigning the exact IP address thus preserving on IP address pool to be used even when it can only provide about 4 million total ips.
-- b) ipv6 is still prevailing and it also uses such protocol thus , dynamic IP is available in both ipv4 and ipv6.
-- c) use command **ip addr**
--list
++n img class="w3-image w3-block" src="res/images/cyber_security/1.png"
--n
++list
##### OSI model
- Physical - wires, cat6
- data - switching, Mac address
- network - routing, IP address
- transport - tcp, udp
- session -  session management
- presentation - webm, gif
- application - http, smtp
--list

#### Notes
- If you want to test out your skills while try to earn money for it, do checkout bugcrowd.com , where many corporations provide their request to find bugs in their web platform.
- **For finding email addresses**
-- 1) hunter.io lets you find email addresses of personals related some website domain, and their positions and comfirmity of such informations and pattern if possible.
-- 2) phonebook.cz 
-- 3) voilanorbert.com
-- 4) clearbit connect chrome extension ( recommended )
- **For verifying email addresses**
-- 1) verifyemailaddress.io
-- 2) email-checker.net/validate
-- 3) just try out to forget password in Gmail login
-- 4) dehashed.com will give you more than just email, could give you password, hashed password ...
--list
++list
##### Domains and names
- 1) sublist3r, searches the domain in every search engines
- 2) crt.sh searches every website available in that domain, e.g. %.tesla.com
- 3) tomnomnom/httpprob helps to check which websites are alive
- 4) builtwith.com has a lot of analysis and tool tracking capabilities
- 5) wappalyzer extension gives you info on what technology the website is relying upon
- 6) whatweb terminal tool is kind of similar as wappalyzer
- 7) berp suite desktop application, intersects how a website is handled on web and thus provides with a lot more informations.
- 8) use Google, e.g.
-- a) site: nic.gov.np filetype:pdf , finds every PDF in site nic.gov.np
-- b) site: gov.np filetype:pdf, finds every site that contains gov.np and their related pdfs
--list
++list
##### tools
- 1) netdiscover , helps find range of network that is available, given an IP and bitmask
- 2) nmap , helps scan live ports of a network provided
- 3) nikto , helps us find about hosts website information
- 4) dirbuster, gobuster, ffuf all help busting for directories indexing in a website as a vunrability issue
- 5) msf, console tool helps in exploitation of smb or ...
- 6) smbclient, to connect to smb
- 7) searchsploit, terminal tool helps us to search for kinds of exploits that we can do for specific version of softwares
- 8) nessus essentials
- 9) openLuck helps us exploit through the vunurabilities of a software in a system
- 10) hydra, terminal tool is used for brute force attack on ssh to try and connect to shell for exploitation purpose.
- 11) immunity debugger is a cool program that helps us check what's going under the hood as the code for exploitation is running
-- a) mona command helps us find modules inside a program using immunity debugger
- 12) msfvenom , shell tool helps us generate the shell code for "shell codes so that we can apply it to buffer overflow" for exploitation.
- 13) fcrakezip, crakes zips with password
- 14) GTFOBins, contains a number of small binaries that help to break across security
--list
++p
